PullRequest.Title: sessions: add Codicon confetti easter egg
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

- Turn one random Codicon background cell into an accessible Celebrate button.
- Launch confetti and move the target after each activation without changing icon geometry.
- Keep targets fully visible and away from foreground composer controls.
- Respect reduced motion, announce activation, and record discovery telemetry.

## Testing

- `npm run transpile-client`
- `npm run typecheck-client`
- Targeted ESLint for the renderer and chat view tests
- 56 affected unit tests
- Agents Window E2E: 250 consecutive target transfers with zero foreground overlaps; physical click verified confetti, stable geometry, and target movement

## Demo

Mouse and keyboard activation launch confetti and transfer the hidden target without moving the Codicon cells.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed event registrations, SessionsPart ownership, synchronous call path, grid/control nested loops, and pre-diff absence are explicit. RunOnceScheduler coalesces same-turn events but does not remove recurring per-frame scroll or streaming updates; exact frame cost varies with viewport and visible control count.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Main-thread DOM traversal, DOMRect/layout reads, and cell-by-occluder intersection CPU work
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Each coalesced refresh traverses the sessions subtree, reads a DOMRect for every discovered control, then checks every visible Codicon cell against those controls: O(D + C×O), where C grows with viewport area and O/D grow with visible chat/session DOM. Captured scroll and streaming DOM updates can trigger one refresh per event-loop/frame.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Increased main-thread CPU and forced-layout risk during transcript rendering and scrolling, causing input/scroll latency and dropped frames on large or split chat views.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before the PR, the renderer observed only the sessions part's size. renderCodicons returned immediately when the 80px grid dimensions were unchanged, so transcript scrolling and ordinary chat DOM mutations performed no background geometry work.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The added subtree MutationObserver schedules a refresh for class/style/child-list changes anywhere outside the background, and the added captured scroll listener does the same for descendant scrollers. renderCodicons now calls getConfettiCandidateGeometry before its unchanged-grid early return, scanning the full subtree and synchronously reading every occluder's bounds on every such refresh.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT lines 185-195 newly register subtree mutation and captured scroll invalidations; previously only the root ResizeObserver called renderCodicons. The diff also moves expensive candidate geometry ahead of the unchanged-grid return, so these new events cannot take the old constant-time early exit.
Findings.Title: Avoid full occluder recomputation on chat scroll and mutation
Findings.Impact: With the Codicons background selected, scrolling a transcript or streaming/virtualizing a response repeatedly runs the full geometry pass on the UI thread. A default 960×800 background has roughly 107 cells; a 4K part has roughly 1,150, and each is compared with every visible link/button/input/role-based control across all split sessions.
Findings.Evidence: SessionsPart constructs this renderer with interactive=true. Added lines 185-195 observe the entire part subtree and all captured descendant scrolls. The scheduled callback calls renderCodicons; line 224 invokes getConfettiCandidateGeometry before the grid-size equality check at line 252. Lines 295-310 recursively enumerate foreground descendants and call getBoundingClientRect for each, while lines 322-327 compare each candidate cell against every collected rectangle. ChatView embeds the scrolling ChatWidget tree in this same SessionsPart, and ChatWidget auto-scrolls while responses render.
Findings.Recommendation: Do not rebuild all candidates on every descendant scroll/mutation. Keep structural candidate rebuilding on bounded geometry changes, validate only the current target on scrolling (for example with a point hit-test), and scope observation to the known foreground/composer surfaces; preserve target transfer only when that validation fails.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The allocation site is explicitly inside the viewport-cell loop, SessionsPart always enables the interactive branch, and only one resulting element is activated. The exact latency varies by display size, but the object/listener cardinality and retention are deterministic.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Button objects, emitters, focus trackers, event listeners, disposable graphs, and extra DOM nodes retained for decorative cells
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Allocation grows with the full viewport grid, approximately 8/9 × ceil(width/80) × ceil(height/80): about 107 cells at the 960×800 fallback and about 1,150 at 3840×2160, although only one cell can be active.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Higher Codicons-background creation/resize latency plus persistent DOM/listener memory and later disposal/GC pressure while the background is selected.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Each visible cell was one renderIcon HTMLElement with no per-cell controller, focus tracker, emitter, or listeners.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The loop now calls createCodiconButton for every interactive-renderer cell. Each call constructs a full base Button, an animation wrapper and icon, a DisposableStore, and a per-cell onDidClick subscription; Button itself creates click/tap/keydown/mouseover/mouseout and focus-tracking machinery, even though CSS disables pointer events and tabindex for every inactive cell.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 276 replaces the old one-renderIcon-per-cell path with createCodiconButton for every cell in the interactive renderer; the added implementation at line 343 instantiates the heavyweight Button. Before this diff no Button or per-cell event machinery existed.
Findings.Title: Keep inactive Codicon cells lightweight
Findings.Impact: Selecting the Codicons background eagerly constructs hundreds—and on a full 4K sessions part over a thousand—full Button instances and their listener/disposable graphs for a feature with exactly one interactive target. This blocks the initial background render and retains the overhead until the background changes or the part is disposed.
Findings.Evidence: Line 276 is inside the visibleCells loop and chooses createCodiconButton for every cell because SessionsPart passes interactive=true. createCodiconButton at lines 341-361 constructs Button plus wrapper/icon and click subscription. Base Button's constructor registers gesture support, click, tap, keydown, mouseover, mouseout, and focus/blur tracking. updateConfettiButtons marks only cell===confettiCell active and makes every other cell tabindex=-1, aria-hidden, and pointer-events:none.
Findings.Recommendation: Render inactive cells as the previous lightweight icon/cell elements and keep only the current target interactive, or use one delegated click/keydown handler on the Codicon layer while toggling role/tabindex/class on the selected lightweight cell. This preserves stable geometry and target transfer without per-cell Button controllers.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open or resize the Sessions part with the Codicons background selected
Scenarios.CriticalPath: setBackground/renderCodicons runs synchronously on the renderer/UI thread before the background is ready; resize notifications are deferred through a zero-delay RunOnceScheduler but their render remains on the UI critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create and attach the Codicon DOM grid and per-cell Button controllers/listeners
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One full Button/controller graph for every non-skipped grid cell, despite one active target
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: One renderIcon HTMLElement per cell with no Button controller or per-cell listeners
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous DOM/object allocation blocks background creation and grid growth

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read background and foreground-control DOMRect geometry
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One background read plus one getBoundingClientRect per discovered visible control per refresh
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous layout/style resolution occurs before candidate selection

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The 80px grid has approximately 8/9 × ceil(width/80) × ceil(height/80) cells: about 107 at 960×800 and about 1,150 at 3840×2160.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One SessionsChatBackgroundRenderer serializes work on the browser main thread. RunOnceScheduler coalesces overlapping invalidations but does not parallelize allocation or geometry work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: codiconCells reuses existing cells while the grid dimensions stay unchanged, and foregroundResizeObservations reuses observations by element. Cold render allocates all cells; warm same-grid renders avoid cell recreation but still rebuild candidate geometry and candidate sets before the early return.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the per-cell allocation loop, Button implementation, synchronous ownership, and old lightweight implementation are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact latency depends on display size, device speed, and the number of split/visible chats, but viewport-scaled Button/listener cardinality is deterministic.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable eager-work regression: all decorative cells receive heavyweight interactive machinery.

Scenarios.Scenario: Scroll a transcript or stream/render a response while the Codicons background is selected
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Captured descendant scrolls and subtree mutation batches schedule renderCodicons; its full candidate geometry pass runs on the main thread alongside scrolling, list virtualization, and response rendering.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Traverse the Sessions part, synchronously read every occluder's DOMRect, and compare every candidate cell with every occluder
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one coalesced pass per mutation/scroll scheduling window; within a pass, O(D + C×O) work
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Transcript mutations and scrolling did not invoke the background renderer; only root resize did, and unchanged grid dimensions returned before collection work
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs on the scroll/render main-thread path and can force layout after DOM mutations

ExpensiveBoundaries.Location: Existing ChatWidget/provider response path reached by src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/browser/chatView.ts
ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Deliver the existing chat response stream that causes transcript updates
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Pre-existing streamed updates per response; exact provider transport and chunk count vary
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same streamed updates rendered the transcript without triggering full background occluder recomputation
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The boundary itself is unchanged, but each resulting render/mutation now drives the added local geometry pass

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Visible sessions subtree size D, discovered controls O, and Codicon cells C. Each refresh is O(D + C×O); split sessions and larger viewports increase all three effective cardinalities.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Mutation records are browser-batched and RunOnceScheduler coalesces same-window bursts, but recurring scroll/render frames each schedule serialized main-thread work with no limiter across frames.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No candidate-geometry cache is used: the subtree, DOMRects, candidate set, and intersections are rebuilt each refresh. ResizeObserver registrations are reused, but that does not avoid the scan or layout reads.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: SessionsPart passes interactive=true, the observers cover the ChatWidget subtree, and geometry is executed before the unchanged-grid early return.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Visible control count, streaming cadence, and browser layout cost vary; the per-refresh nested scaling and reachability from scroll/mutation are certain.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable synchronous UI regression: repeated full geometry work is newly attached to active scroll and response-render paths.

Scenarios.Scenario: Activate the Celebrate target with mouse or keyboard
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The click/key handler synchronously fires activation, starts a small compositor animation unless reduced motion is enabled, announces status, logs telemetry, selects another candidate, updates cell attributes, and may transfer focus.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Submit an empty-payload publicLog2 telemetry event
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous API invocation is on activation, but the payload is constant and bounded; downstream transport is not awaited

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create 11 temporary animation elements and Web Animations, then remove the overlay
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one active overlay globally; ten particles plus one ring per accepted activation
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: User-triggered and bounded; reduced-motion users skip it

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One activation at a time; target update loops over the viewport cell count and candidate selection copies the candidate set.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The animation helper permits one global active overlay, so repeated rapid activations do not create concurrent overlays. Attribute updates are synchronous on the UI thread.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The existing confettiCandidates set is reused for selection; no remote/cache lookup is involved. The overlay is removed after two seconds.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: activation code and animation cleanup are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Activation frequency is user-controlled, but overlay concurrency and payload size are bounded.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional reportable regression: activation animation and telemetry are bounded and user-triggered; per-cell update cost is dominated by the separately reported eager cell design.

Scenarios.Scenario: Use Sessions with no background or an image background
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The new subtree and scroll observers still schedule renderCodicons, but renderCodicons immediately returns because background.kind is not codicons.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Mutation/scroll event frequency only; no subtree geometry scan or cell loop occurs in this mode.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: RunOnceScheduler coalesces scheduling on the main thread.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: clearCodicons releases cells/observations when leaving Codicons mode; no candidate cache remains.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the background-kind guard is the first statement in renderCodicons.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The callback/scheduler overhead depends on UI activity but is constant per coalesced delivery and has no geometry work.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression in non-Codicons modes; the residual observer scheduling is small and bounded.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all seven changed files. Submitted two findings: repeated main-thread full-tree/layout work on chat scroll/mutation, and eager heavyweight Button allocation for every decorative Codicon cell. Checked activation animation/telemetry, cleanup, caching, resize/mutation coalescing, concurrency, and non-Codicons behavior; no performance regression fix was identified.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
